name: Exact Classification of Obstructions with a Separating Edge
statement: Let irredundantly embedded ample pieces with connected nonempty exclusive parts share an edge $D$, and let $X$ be their union. Then $X$ is a pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness exactly when: (1) there are two or three pieces, every piece is dismantlable ample, and none peels to $D$; (2) two pieces are mutually incompatible, while with three pieces every pair is compatible; (3) every zero-side restriction or contraction in an exclusive coordinate either makes the changed piece peel to $D$ or, in the two-piece case, makes it compatible with the unchanged piece, whereas in the three-piece case it must peel to $D$; and (4) in each shared-coordinate restriction or contraction, at most one image fails to peel to the resulting singleton. Every obstruction with a specified separating edge arises uniquely this way, and the union is two-connected exactly when every piece is two-connected.
proof: The separating-cube bound gives two or three positive relative-failing pieces. The edge-gluing criterion makes a two-piece obstruction incompatible, while every proper two-piece subunion of a three-piece obstruction must be compatible. Exclusive-coordinate minor minimality is exactly the stated edge-profile alternative; shared-coordinate images reduce to the one-point-amalgam criterion. Conversely these conditions make the original union nonpeelable and every elementary image peelable. Components outside the marked edge recover the pieces and their coordinate blocks. Deleting a vertex disconnects the union exactly when it disconnects one piece away from the still-shared endpoint or edge.
